/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 51-year-old man comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of dizziness, tinnitus, and hearing loss on the left side for 6 weeks. These episodes last for hours at a time and are associated with the sensation that the room is spinning. He has no history of major medical illness and takes no medications. Examination shows horizontal nystagmus to the left. Weber test shows lateralization to the right ear. The Rinne test is positive bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

Options:
A. Dislodged otoliths
B. Inflammation of the vestibular nerve
C. Acoustic neuroma
D. Endolymphatic hydrops
E. Posterior inferior cerebellar artery infarction

text: {"in_scope": false, "reason": "The question pertains to otologic/vestibular pathology (e.g., Ménière's disease) rather than mental health or psychiatric disorders."}
